title: Dominic and the Asset
premise: Jonah Sandoval, a veteran interpreter for a faltering peace delegation, discovers that a diplomatic flight carrying a key witness has been erased from every record while still airborne — and that the witness was trained by a covert network Jonah's own government quietly funds. As the summit approaches, Jonah is recruited, threatened, and finally weaponized by factions inside the machine he serves. To survive, he must turn his linguistic skills into an instrument of exposure, burning the training network from within before the delegates convene. The story ends with the summit saved in name only: the network destroyed, but at the cost of Jonah's career, his safety, and his belief that any institution can hold power without corrupting it.
about_author: Dominic Voss spent a decade working as a contract linguist on international delegations before turning to fiction full-time. He writes thrillers about the people who translate power — and what happens when they start translating it honestly.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Obedience
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. On the eve of a fragile peace summit, Jonah interprets a preliminary session where a delegate's words are deliberately mistranslated by his own team to protect a deal. He complies, hating himself. Emotional beat: quiet complicity, the first crack in his faith in procedure.

chapters.title: Flight 114
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A chartered flight carrying Marek Ilves, a defector willing to testify about a clandestine training program, goes silent mid-route. Within hours, manifests, radar logs, and passenger lists vanish. Jonah, who interpreted Ilves's intake interview years ago, receives a summons at midnight. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Records Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In a windowless records office, Jonah watches an archivist deny Flight 114 ever existed — then slip him a printed fragment when no one is looking. The fragment names a facility: Kestrel House. Beat: the vertigo of gaslighting, and the first ally.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Marek (flashback interleaved). Seven years earlier, Ilves arrives at Kestrel House, a 'language school' that trains interpreters to reshape meaning under pressure. He excels until he refuses an assignment. Beat: the seduction of belonging curdling into captivity; memory as contested ground.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A woman named Ada Reyes presents herself as internal oversight and recruits Jonah to trace the flight's erasure. Her credentials check out perfectly — too perfectly. Jonah accepts anyway. Beat: wary alliance, the reader sensing the trap before he does.

chapters.title: Kestrel House
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Following the fragment, Jonah travels to a decommissioned estate now listed as a private academy. He finds sanitized classrooms, shredded files, and a caretaker who recognizes Ilves's photograph and immediately stops speaking. Beat: physical evidence that the past is being actively buried.

chapters.title: Terms of Art
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Back at the delegation, Jonah decodes bureaucratic euphemisms in leaked cables — 'linguistic calibration,' 'narrative assurance' — mapping the network's vocabulary. Each term maps to an operation. Beat: intellectual momentum; his craft becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Second Interpreter
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A colleague, Tomas Brandt, warns Jonah off, revealing he once worked a Kestrel-adjacent posting and was broken by it. That night someone searches Jonah's apartment. Beat: fear made domestic; loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Her chapter reveals she is not oversight but the network's cleaner, tasked with managing Jonah — or eliminating him. Yet reviewing his file, she hesitates: he reminds her of the recruit she once was. Beat: antagonist interiority; corruption shown from inside.

chapters.title: Ilves Lives
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A dead-drop message in Ilves's old cipher reaches Jonah: the flight landed; Ilves is held at a black site near the coast, alive because his testimony is still useful to one faction. Beat: hope rekindled, stakes doubled.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. With nine days until the summit, Jonah realizes both sides want Ilves silenced before he can testify — the network to hide its crimes, the host government to protect its funding. Beat: claustrophobic countdown; no safe side.

chapters.title: Coastal Road
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah drives to the black site posing as a contracted interpreter, using genuine credentials from his old postings. He gets inside, sees Ilves through glass — and is recognized by a Kestrel instructor. Beat: audacity rewarded, then punished.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Captured, Jonah is interrogated by the very techniques Kestrel taught: linguistic traps, false-memory seeding. He survives by doing what he does best — listening for the seams in their script. Beat: his skill set saves his life; memory under assault.

chapters.title: The Deal in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ordered to dispose of Jonah, Ada instead offers him a bargain: her testimony on the network in exchange for extraction for them both. She admits she erased the flight's records — on orders she no longer believes in. Beat: betrayal inverted into alliance.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A brutal night operation frees Ilves; Brandt, redeeming himself, provides the route and dies covering their retreat. Beat: sacrifice, grief, forward motion at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Safehouse Cipher
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Hidden outside the city, Jonah and Ilves reconstruct the network's structure from memory and documents: twelve nodes, three funders, one director — a man scheduled to chair the summit's security committee. Beat: the map completes; the target revealed.

chapters.title: What We Trained You For
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Ilves confesses his role: he didn't just witness the program, he helped build its curriculum. His defection was penance. Jonah must decide whether a compromised witness is still a weapon worth firing. Beat: moral reckoning; justice vs. purity.

chapters.title: Six Hours
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Six hours before the opening session, the trio splits: Ada takes the funders' ledger to two journalists, Ilves prepares to walk into the hall, and Jonah goes after the director with a recording of the interrogation — of himself. Beat: coiled tension before detonation.

chapters.title: The Opening Session
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. As delegates rise, Ilves enters uninvited and begins to testify aloud. Security moves; Jonah simultaneously broadcasts the recordings to every delegate's terminal via the interpretation system itself — the network's own channel turned against it. Beat: climax; language as liberation.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The director tries to contain the leak; Ada releases the ledger publicly, ending her usefulness to anyone and painting a target on herself. The network fractures in real time as funders flee. Beat: fire spreading; no clean hands.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Interpreted
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Weeks later, inquiries open, headlines fade, and the summit concludes with a hollow agreement everyone calls historic. Jonah testifies, is thanked, and is quietly blacklisted. Beat: bitter victory; justice achieved outside the law, unrewarded by it.

chapters.title: A New Sentence
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In a small coastal town, Jonah works as a translator for refugees, anonymous and unregretful. Ada sends a postcard with no return address; Ilves teaches languages openly. Jonah begins writing down everything he remembers. Beat: resolution — memory preserved, self remade, vigilance ongoing.
